reasons: The tests were read, not run, so passing status is not confirmed.
Error message matching makes the tests sensitive to wording changes.

terms.meaning: the way an assumption is dealt with: proven by evidence, named as a prerequisite, or left unsupported
a check that runs automatically when data is created, and refuses data that breaks a rule
an unsupported assumption that the design depends on, which lowers its confidence
set so that its values cannot be changed after creation

used_by: the pytest run for the schema tests

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for assumption tests
sections.what: Imports pytest, the validation error type and the assumption types from the schema package.
sections.why: The tests need these to build assumptions and check the errors they raise.

sections.name: prerequisite
sections.title: Building a valid prerequisite
sections.what: Builds a complete declared prerequisite, with a name, a type and an evidence citation, and lets a test change any field.
sections.why: Many tests need a valid prerequisite as a starting point and then change one field to check a rule.
sections.watch_out: The default name and evidence id are fixed sample values, so a test that depends on a specific value must set it explicitly.

sections.name: assumption
sections.title: Building a valid assumption
sections.what: Builds an unsupported assumption with a statement, no citation and a claim reference, and lets a test override any field.
sections.why: Most assumption tests start here and change one field to see whether the rule holds.

sections.name: TestTheResolutionMustBeTheThingItClaims (part 1)
sections.title: Resolution rules and their costs
sections.what: Checks that a grounded assumption needs a citation, an unsupported one cannot carry a citation, and a declared prerequisite must be named, typed and cited. The refusal for a missing citation points to the unsupported resolution as the honest option.
sections.why: Each resolution must cost something. If a prerequisite could be declared without evidence, every hard assumption would be filed there.
sections.watch_out: The tests match exact phrases in error messages, so changing that wording will break them.

sections.name: TestTheResolutionMustBeTheThingItClaims: test_naming_a_prerequisite_on_another_resolution_is_refused
sections.title: Prerequisite refused on the wrong resolution
sections.what: Checks that naming a prerequisite on an assumption whose resolution is not declared prerequisite is refused.
sections.why: Such a prerequisite would not appear in the ordering of work and would not be scheduled, so it would look recorded but have no effect.

sections.name: TestOnlyUnsupportedCostsCoverage
sections.title: Only unsupported assumptions count as gaps
sections.what: Checks that an unsupported assumption is a load-bearing gap, while a declared prerequisite and a grounded assumption are not.
sections.why: Penalising a named dependency would make it cheaper to leave a dependency unnamed, which is the opposite of what the system is for.
sections.watch_out: Changing this rule changes confidence scores everywhere they are calculated.

sections.name: TestTheVocabularyIsClosed
sections.title: The set of allowed values is closed
sections.what: Checks that there are exactly three resolutions, that unknown resolutions are refused, that empty statements are refused, that the evidence list must be given, and that an assumption cannot be changed after creation.
sections.why: A fourth state such as under investigation would let an assumption sit without any cost, and the docstring says it was rejected for that reason.
sections.watch_out: Adding a resolution requires changing this test on purpose.

sections.name: TestUnprompted
sections.title: Assumption with no prompting objection
sections.what: Checks that an assumption can exist without a claim reference, meaning it was declared before anyone objected.
sections.why: The docstring calls this the better case and says it should be possible to count it.

sections.name: TestAnAssumptionCannotNameItsOwnDesign (part 1)
sections.title: Helper for a design that names its own parts
sections.what: Builds a complete future design with one step, one agent and one assumption whose prerequisite name is supplied by the test.
sections.why: A design cannot be its own prerequisite. A dependency pointing back at its own design looks like a cycle to the planner and fails the whole portfolio for a reason nobody can see.
sections.watch_out: This helper builds a whole valid design, so a required field added to the design will break every test that uses it.

sections.name: TestAnAssumptionCannotNameItsOwnDesign: test_naming_a_step_of_this_design_is_refused
sections.title: Self-reference refused, outside names accepted
sections.what: Checks that naming a step or an agent from the same design as a prerequisite is refused, that naming something outside the design is accepted, and that an accepted prerequisite does not count as a gap.
sections.why: The check must not fire on ordinary cases, or it becomes unusable and someone would remove it.
sections.watch_out: The refusal test matches an exact phrase in the error message.

summary: Tests the rules for declared assumptions, which record what a design takes for granted and how that is resolved.
purpose: Makes sure every assumption has the right resolution, cost and citation, and that a design cannot name its own parts as a prerequisite.
why: The docstrings say an assumption that can be asserted without cost would turn the whole mechanism into a simple disclosure. Each rule closes a route to hiding a hard assumption.
how: Builds sample assumptions and prerequisites with a few overrides, then checks each validation rule with a test that expects an error or an acceptance. A helper builds a full future design so the self-reference rule can be tested.
inputs: Sample values built inside the file. The real values come from the packages.schema package.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. The tests make no files.
risks: Several tests match exact error wording, so rewording a validation message will break them. Changing the list of resolutions or the cost rule changes results everywhere.
debug: If a test fails with an unexpected accept or refusal, check the validators in packages.schema for the assumption and future state classes. If a message match fails, compare the new wording with the expected phrase in the test.
